porbos.title: The Tribes’ Request • Treachery in the Pass • Khubayb’s Last Two Rak‘ahs

blocks.1: A few months passed after Uhud. Shawwal, Dhu al-Qa‘dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, Muharram. Madinah had some relief then. At that time two delegations from two tribes came to Madinah. One from the tribes of ‘Adal and al-Qarah, the other from the tribe of ‘Amir ibn Sa‘sa‘ah. Both groups said almost the same thing: Islam is spreading among us, send some of your Companions, they will teach us the religion and have us recite the Qur’an.{{1}}
blocks.2: The Prophet {{1}} accepted both requests. With the first group he sent ten Companions. With the second, seventy.{{2}}
blocks.3: Both groups had lied. An eagerness to learn the religion; few requests sound more beautiful. Precisely behind this cover lay the deepest conspiracy. The Prophet {{1}} believed, because treachery was not in his nature; he had never learned to search for a plot in anyone’s word. When we are deceived once, afterwards we look for suspicion in everyone’s words. Yet another’s deceit can never be a reason for changing our own honesty.
blocks.5: The leader of those who went with ‘Adal and al-Qarah was ‘Asim ibn Thabit (RA). With him were Khubayb ibn ‘Adi (RA), Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah (RA), ‘Abdullah ibn Tariq (RA) and a few others. Although they were called with talk of teaching the religion, this group entering unfamiliar territory is described in the hadith as a reconnaissance expedition; after Uhud, caution was only natural. As soon as they reached a watering place of Hudhayl named Raji‘, the group betrayed them; those they had called to teach the religion shouted and brought Hudhayl, to attack their own guests.{{1}}
blocks.7: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} sent ten men as a scouting party, and appointed as their commander ‘Asim ibn Thabit al-Ansari, the grandfather of ‘Asim ibn ‘Umar. They set out, and when they reached a place called al-Hada’ah between ‘Usfan and Makkah, news of them was given to a branch of Hudhayl called Banu Lihyan. About two hundred men, all archers, followed them, tracing their marks, even seeing the date stones they had left behind and saying, these are the dates of Madinah. In the end they caught up with them.{{2}}
blocks.8: ‘Asim (RA) and his companions took refuge on a high mound. The enemy surrounded them and said, come down, we promise you, we will not kill even one. ‘Asim (RA) said, I will not come down today under the protection of a disbeliever. O Allah, inform Your Prophet of our news. They shot arrows. ‘Asim (RA) was martyred with seven others. Left were Khubayb (RA), Zayd (RA), and a third, ‘Abdullah ibn Tariq (RA).{{1}}
blocks.9: ‘Asim’s (RA) prayer was accepted that very day. The news reached the Prophet {{1}} of what had happened to ‘Asim (RA) and his companions.{{2}}
blocks.10: At Badr, two sons of Sulafah bint Sa‘d, a woman of Makkah, had been killed by ‘Asim (RA). In revenge she had vowed to drink wine from ‘Asim’s (RA) skull.{{1}}
blocks.12: When some disbelievers of Quraysh heard that ‘Asim (RA) had been killed, they sent men to bring some part of his body, so he could be recognized; because on the day of Badr he had killed one of their great leaders. But Allah sent a swarm of insects, like a cloud, over ‘Asim (RA), which protected him from their messenger; they could not cut anything from his flesh.{{1}}
blocks.13: In his lifetime ‘Asim (RA) had vowed that no polytheist would touch him, and he would not touch any polytheist. When ‘Umar (RA) heard that the bees had protected his body, he would say, Allah protects His believing servant.{{1}}
blocks.14: ‘Asim (RA) kept one vow all his life. After his death Allah kept that same vow for him. The vow we forget, assuming no one will remember, that is exactly what Allah remembers.
blocks.16: Khubayb (RA), Zayd (RA) and the third softened, surrendered in hope of living, on the condition of a word and a promise. The word was not kept. They were bound with bowstrings and taken away. The third freed his hands and said, this is the first betrayal. He refused to go along. They pulled and tugged but could not persuade him; they stoned him and killed him right there.
blocks.18: They took Khubayb (RA) and Ibn al-Dathinnah away, and sold them in Makkah after the Battle of Badr. The sons of al-Harith ibn ‘Amir ibn Nawfal bought Khubayb (RA); on the day of Badr it was Khubayb (RA) who had killed al-Harith ibn ‘Amir. Khubayb (RA) remained a captive with them.{{1}}
blocks.19: Month after month he remained a captive. Al-Harith’s daughter herself later used to narrate those days.
blocks.21: When they gathered to kill him, he asked me to lend him a razor, to cleanse his body. I lent it to him. Meanwhile one of my sons, without my noticing, had gone to him. I saw the boy sitting on his lap, the razor in his hand. I was so startled that Khubayb (RA) understood it from my face. He said, are you afraid I will kill him? I would not do that. By Allah, I have never seen a better captive than Khubayb (RA). By Allah, one day I saw him eating from a bunch of grapes in his hand, though he was bound in iron, and there was no fruit anywhere in Makkah. It was surely provision from Allah, which He had given to Khubayb (RA).{{1}}
blocks.22: A captive who would be killed in a few days, in his hand a sharp razor and an innocent child. The mother, watching from a distance, gasped. Yet in the captive’s mind there was not the slightest evil thought toward the child. The person who even in the last moments of their life guards another’s trust needs no further proof of their character. There was no fruit anywhere in Makkah, yet in his hand a bunch of grapes. Even when all the doors of people close, Allah’s door does not close. Allah had not forgotten even the provision of a prisoner in chains. In the end he was taken away to be killed.
blocks.24: When they took him out of the Haram to kill him, Khubayb (RA) said to them, let me pray two rak‘ahs. They let him go, and he prayed two rak‘ahs. Then he said, by Allah, were it not that you would think I am prolonging this out of fear of death, I would have prolonged it more. O Allah, count them one by one. And I do not care, so long as I die a Muslim, on whichever side my body falls in the way of Allah. This is for Allah alone; if He wills, He will bless every severed limb of my torn body. Then Ibn al-Harith stood up and killed him. Standing before death, Khubayb (RA) was the first Muslim who established this practice of two rak‘ahs for every Muslim killed as a captive.{{1}}
blocks.25: Before being crucified Khubayb (RA) also said some words, in the rhythm of poetry.
blocks.27: To Allah I complain of my loneliness, then my distress, and of what the enemies have prepared for me at my death. The fear of death does not make me tremble, I will die anyway; my fear is only of the blazing fire of Hell.{{1}}
blocks.28: One who can speak of his loneliness even before death, it would be wrong to say there was no fear in his heart. There was fear, but the place of that fear was right. Not the death of the world, but the fire of the Hereafter. A deed begins from need, then becomes a custom. Two rak‘ahs before a martyr, still in this Ummah’s memory. Mu‘awiyah (RA), still a polytheist then, was in the crowd that day. Later he used to say, hearing Khubayb’s (RA) curse I lay down on the ground in fear.{{1}}
blocks.29: Another was Sa‘id ibn ‘Amir (RA), still a polytheist then. Many years later he was an amir appointed by ‘Umar (RA) in Syria. Once the people of Hims went to ‘Umar (RA) and made four complaints against their amir: that he comes out only after much of the day has passed, that he does not answer anyone’s call at night, that one day a month he does not show himself at all, and that now and then he faints. ‘Umar (RA) asked the reasons one by one. Sa‘id (RA) said, I have no servant; I knead the dough myself, bake the bread, then come out, so I am late. I have kept the day for the people, and the night I have kept only for the worship of Allah. And that one day a month, I have only one garment, I am delayed in coming out waiting for it to be washed and dried. Then the answer to the fourth complaint: in Makkah I saw Khubayb’s death scene with my own eyes. Quraysh was wounding his body with knives, yet asked, would you want Muhammad in your place? He said, by Allah, I would not want to sit among my family while even a thorn pricks Muhammad {{1}}. That day I did not help him; that memory is what sometimes makes me faint.{{2}}
blocks.30: Hearing all four answers ‘Umar (RA) was pleased and sent a thousand dinars in Sa‘id’s (RA) name. Sa‘id (RA) gave away all of it among widows, orphans and the needy, keeping with himself only one gold coin. An ordinary subject complaining to the caliph about his appointed amir, the caliph listening attentively to that complaint, summoning the amir to account; this very scene is a picture of ‘Umar’s (RA) rule. A scene can haunt a person all their life. That day Sa‘id (RA) was a polytheist; later he accepted Islam, and became ‘Umar’s (RA) beloved amir too. Yet the weight of that scene did not lift.

Since both were asked the same question, both may have given answers of the same pattern, or the names may have been swapped in the narration; which is correct cannot be said with certainty, so both narrations have been kept independently.

quiz.q: After Uhud, which two tribes sent delegations to Madinah asking for Companions?
o: ‘Adal-al-Qarah and ‘Amir ibn Sa‘sa‘ah
Banu Lihyan and Banu Sulaym
Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qurayzah
Ri‘l, Dhakwan, ‘Usayyah and Banu Lihyan

quiz.q: Though the ‘Adal-al-Qarah tribe asked for Companions in the name of learning da‘wah, what was their real aim?
o: Really learning the religion and returning to their own tribe
Building a permanent alliance with Madinah
Handing them over to Quraysh to receive a reward
Asking for some weapons for use in war

quiz.q: From the incident of the Raji‘ expedition, what caution can be taken in today’s life?
o: Every offer of help should be rejected without consideration
To regard every stranger with suspicion
To trust only those of blood relation
Not to trust without verifying merely because someone’s offer sounds sweet
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3045; Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir.

quiz.q: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, how many were in the party of ‘Asim ibn Thabit (RA)?
o: Six
Ten
Forty
Seventy

quiz.q: What did Allah send to protect ‘Asim’s body?
o: A fierce storm
A guarding band of angels
A swarm of insects like bees
Heavy rain for several days in a row

quiz.q: What lay behind ‘Asim (RA) refusing to surrender?
o: The prospect of victory still looking bright
A strict instruction received from companions before the fight began
A fierce desire to take revenge on the enemy
A resolve not to rely on the promise of any disbeliever

quiz.q: Though the polytheists wanted to mutilate ‘Asim’s body, why could they not?
o: A swarm of insects like bees stood guard around the body
In the deep darkness of night the body was moved away somewhere
The companions guarded the body all night
The polytheists became frightened and left the place

quiz.q: What lesson does ‘Asim’s (RA) saying ‘I will not come down under a disbeliever’s protection’ give in today’s life?
o: Never to compromise on self-respect and the principles of the religion
To avoid every kind of compromise in life
To refuse others’ help even in time of need
That it is always better to carry on the fight alone

quiz.q: Who bought Khubayb and Zayd in Makkah?
o: Abu Sufyan and his wife Hind bint ‘Utbah
Umayyah ibn Khalaf and his son
Some members of Abu Jahl’s family
The sons of al-Harith and Safwan ibn Umayyah
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 3045; Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir.

quiz.q: What did Khubayb ask for before death?
o: Permission to pray two rak‘ahs
Permission to send a letter to his family
Permission to drink water
Time to write poetry

quiz.q: According to the hadith, who established the practice of two rak‘ahs for a Muslim killed as a captive?
o: ‘Asim ibn Thabit (RA)
Khubayb ibn ‘Adi (RA)
Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah (RA)
‘Abdullah ibn Tariq (RA)

quiz.q: What was the main reason al-Harith’s family bought Khubayb?
o: To make him an ordinary slave and sell him again
The desire to take revenge for al-Harith, killed at Badr
To collect a large ransom in time
To extract news of Madinah from him

quiz.q: What does the scene of a bunch of grapes in Khubayb’s hand, at a time when there was no fruit in Makkah, indicate?
o: He had bought it from the market with his saved money
One of the guards had kindly given it as a gift
It was an inexplicable provision from Allah
He himself had planted a small grapevine

quiz.q: From the request to pray two rak‘ahs before death, what priority of Khubayb is understood?
o: To remember his family one last time
To waste the enemy’s time and look for an opportunity
To postpone the death sentence in hope of help
Placing prayer before everything even at the mouth of death

quiz.q: From Khubayb’s poetry and firmness, what can be learned in today’s hard times?
o: Expressing pain is itself a kind of weakness
To think that protest is always the only right path
One can express steadfastness in faith even amid hardship
It is best to stay completely silent in times of danger

porbos.title: May Not Even a Thorn Pierce • The Seventy Qurra’ • A Month of Invoking Curses

blocks.0: May Not Even a Thorn Pierce
blocks.1: Safwan ibn Umayyah bought Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah (RA), to take revenge for his father. He took him to al-Tan‘im to kill him. A group of people of Makkah gathered to watch, Abu Sufyan among them. Abu Sufyan stood before Zayd (RA) and said, tell me in Allah’s name, Zayd (RA), would you like Muhammad to be in your place now, we cut his neck, and you sit with your family?
blocks.3: By Allah, I would not want Muhammad, in his place, to have even a small thorn prick his foot, while I sit among my family.{{1}}
blocks.4: Abu Sufyan later used to say, I have not seen anyone among people with a love like the love of Muhammad’s Companions for him.{{1}}
blocks.5: Then Zayd (RA) was killed. Khubayb (RA) and Zayd (RA) were martyred on the same day. The Prophet {{1}} had said that day, peace be upon you, Khubayb (RA), Quraysh has killed you.{{2}}
blocks.6: His life was going, yet there was not a word from Zayd’s (RA) mouth for himself. Only one thought, that not even a thorn should touch the Prophet’s {{1}} foot. When we fall into hardship we think first of ourselves. Those who have truly loved think of the safety of the beloved even in their own last moment. The hypocrites were then saying, what did these people get? They neither stayed in their homes, nor could they get the news to the Prophet. Allah revealed verses in answer to them.
blocks.8: And among people there is one whose words about worldly life please you, and he calls Allah to witness as to what is in his heart, yet he is the most hostile of (your) enemies.{{1}}
blocks.10: And (on the other hand) among people there is one who sells his own life to seek the pleasure of Allah. Allah is most compassionate to (such) servants.{{1}}
blocks.11: The same event, two kinds of eyes. In the hypocrite’s eyes, failure; in Allah’s eyes, a life sold, whose price is Allah’s pleasure.{{1}}
blocks.13: A few months after Raji‘ the second group also set out. At the request of Abu Bara’ ‘Amir ibn Malik. Abu Bara’ himself had come to Madinah. He had not become Muslim on hearing about Islam, nor gone far away. He had said, if you send some Companions to the people of Najd, call them, I hope they will respond. The Prophet {{1}} had said, I fear the people of Najd will harm them. Abu Bara’ had said, I am their guarantor.{{2}}
blocks.14: The Prophet {{1}} made Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA) the leader of this group.
blocks.16: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} sent seventy men known as the Qurra’ to help against an enemy. By day they gathered firewood, by night they prayed. When they reached Bi’r Ma‘unah, they were killed, treacherously.{{2}}
blocks.17: Reaching Bi’r Ma‘unah they sent the Prophet’s {{1}} letter to ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl, the nephew of Abu Bara’, in the hand of Haram ibn Milhan (RA), the maternal uncle of Anas (RA). ‘Amir did not even look at the letter; he pounced and killed him at once.{{2}}
blocks.18: At the moment of death Haram (RA) took his own blood in his hand, sprinkled it over his face and head, and said,
blocks.20: I have won, by the Lord of the Ka‘bah.{{1}}
blocks.21: The one being killed says, I have won. Because his reckoning was of the Hereafter, not of the world. A man of ‘Amir’s force later asked, what does ‘I have won’ mean? He was told, Paradise. He said, indeed so. That very day he accepted Islam.{{1}}
blocks.22: Then ‘Amir called the tribe of Banu ‘Amir for help. They said, we will not break Abu Bara’’s promise. ‘Amir then called some clans of Banu Sulaym, Ri‘l, Dhakwan, ‘Usayyah. They agreed. They came and surrounded the remaining Companions. Everyone fought with swords in hand, in the end everyone was martyred. Except one, Ka‘b ibn Zayd, who was left wounded, thought dead. He survived, and was later martyred in the Battle of the Trench.{{1}}
blocks.23: The very words whose meaning Haram (RA) himself understood best at the moment of speaking them later drew even an enemy to the path of Islam. The herd of camels was being grazed away from the camp that day, as every day, to feed on grass; in charge of that herd were ‘Amr ibn Umayyah (RA) and an Ansari Companion of Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf. Because they were away from the camp they survived the attack. Seeing a flock of vultures circling over the camp, they sensed something had happened. Going near, they saw their companions all lying in blood. The Ansari Companion asked, what is your view? ‘Amr (RA) said, let us go to the Prophet {{1}} and tell him. The Ansari Companion said, I will not move from the place where Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA) was martyred; let people never be able to say that I left him alone and ran away. He fought, in the end he was martyred. One was given the chance to leave safely. He refused that chance, because leaving the place of his leader’s martyrdom was, to him, the real danger. Of the chances we seize to avoid trouble, is each one truly safety, or another form of shame? ‘Amr (RA) was taken captive. When he gave his tribe’s name, ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl let him go, in place of one vow of his mother.{{2}}
blocks.24: In that group was ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah (RA), the freed slave of Abu Bakr (RA). He too was killed.
blocks.26: When they were martyred at Bi’r Ma‘unah and ‘Amr ibn Umayyah (RA) was taken captive, ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl pointed to one of the slain and asked ‘Amr, who is this? ‘Amr said, this is ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah (RA). ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl said, I saw that after he was killed he was raised toward the sky, until I could see him between the sky and the earth, then he was laid down on the ground.{{1}}
blocks.27: The news reached Madinah. The Prophet {{1}} announced their martyrdom, saying, your companions were attacked, and they asked their Lord, our Lord, inform our brothers that we are pleased with You and You are pleased with us. The names of ‘Urwah ibn Zubayr and Mundhir ibn Zubayr were later given after ‘Urwah ibn Asma’ and Mundhir ibn ‘Amr (RA), who were martyred that day.{{2}}
blocks.29: On getting the news the Prophet {{1}} was heartbroken. Such grief had not been seen even after Uhud.
blocks.31: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} for a month recited qunut after rising from ruku‘, invoking a curse in the names of some Arab tribes. This was the beginning of qunut, before this we did not recite qunut.{{2}}
blocks.32: Those tribes were Ri‘l, Dhakwan, ‘Usayyah and Banu Lihyan, who had betrayed at Raji‘ and Bi’r Ma‘unah. One month. Every day. The same words. When grief runs so deep, even then the Prophet {{1}} chose the path of du‘a, not of the sword. He did not send an army to take revenge, he only asked of Allah. However, Banu Lihyan’s account was not entirely settled; about two years later there was an expedition against them, that story is for a later dars.{{2}}
blocks.33: Anas (RA) used to say, a verse was revealed about these martyrs, we used to recite it, later it was lifted. Its meaning was: tell our people that we have met our Lord, He is pleased with us, and we are pleased with Him.{{1}}

quiz.q: What question did Abu Sufyan ask Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah?
o: Do you want to abandon Islam and save your life
Where is your family now
Whether he wanted Muhammad in his place or not
Why were you really captured

quiz.q: What was the gist of Zayd’s famous answer?
o: If you free me now I will go straight home to Madinah
I do not actually know Muhammad
I will never forgive you
I do not want even a thorn to prick Muhammad’s foot

quiz.q: Why did Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah use the image of ‘a thorn’ in his answer?
o: Even the slightest pain of the Prophet ﷺ weighed more to him than his own death
He was truly suffering sharply from a thorn wound at that moment
A desire to insult Abu Sufyan in the course of the talk
A trick to waste time because he did not know the answer

quiz.q: What question does Zayd ibn al-Dathinnah’s answer teach us to ask today?
o: Whether it is right to expect a return for love
Whether it is even right to talk with an enemy
Whether fear of death is a natural reaction
How deep my own love for the Prophet ﷺ really is

quiz.q: According to Sahih al-Bukhari, how many Companions were sent to Bi’r Ma‘unah?
o: Seventy
Forty
Sixty
One hundred

quiz.q: What did Haram ibn Milhan (RA) say when speared?
o: Allahu Akbar
Fuztu wa Rabb al-Ka‘bah (I have won, by the Lord of the Ka‘bah)
La ilaha illa Allah
Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji‘un (we belong to Allah and to Him we return)

quiz.q: After the killing of ‘Amir ibn Fuhayrah (RA), what is narrated to have been seen?
o: Light came out of his grave
His blood turned white
His body was raised toward the sky
It is narrated that the smile never left his face

quiz.q: At Bi’r Ma‘unah, what is the difference between Abu Bara’’s (RA) promise and ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl’s act?
o: Both were considered to have given equal full protection in the end
One gave protection, the other himself broke that protection
Both took part together in the betrayal
Abu Bara’ had not made any promise at all

quiz.q: What aspect of the Companions’ way of life shows in their being called ‘Qurra’’?
o: They were attentive all the time only to memorizing the Qur’an
They kept away from all kinds of war
Carrying on together the day’s labour and the night’s long worship
They were people of Madinah’s richest families

quiz.q: What realization shows in Haram ibn Milhan’s (RA) saying ‘fuztu’ (I have won)?
o: Losing consciousness at the moment of intense pain
An attempt to temporarily confuse the enemy
A tactic to keep up the morale of companions behind
Regarding martyrdom not as defeat but as real success

quiz.q: What balance does the ‘Qurra’’ identity of the Bi’r Ma‘unah Companions recall in today’s busy life?
o: Dividing time between livelihood and worship
One should abandon livelihood entirely for worship
One should give all one’s time only to livelihood
Sleep at night is the most important thing in life

quiz.q: How can Haram ibn Milhan’s (RA) ‘fuztu’ change our thinking about death today?
o: Pretending not to fear death at the moment of danger
Learning to regard success in the Hereafter as the real success of life
Forcing a smiling face in every calamity is obligatory
It is better to avoid thinking of death as much as possible

quiz.q: For how long did the Prophet ﷺ invoke curses in qunut against the traitors of Raji‘ and Bi’r Ma‘unah?
o: One week
Three days
Forty days
One month

quiz.q: What was the meaning of the verse revealed about the martyrs of Bi’r Ma‘unah that was later abrogated?
o: We have met our Lord, He is pleased, and we are pleased
Allah has forgiven us and given us a high rank in Paradise
Revenge for our killing will soon be taken
We are not really martyrs, we are still alive

quiz.q: What is understood from the Prophet’s ﷺ invoking curses in qunut for a month?
o: Feeling the pain of betrayal for a long time
Repeatedly failing for a time to control anger
Some new event happening every day
The rules of qunut not yet being settled then

quiz.q: What is understood from the recitation of the verse revealed about the martyrs later being abrogated?
o: It was later proved that this whole event was not actually true
Even if the recitation of some parts of the Qur’an is abrogated, the meaning and rank remain intact
The rank of the martyrs was later reduced
The Companions had forgotten to memorize the verse

quiz.q: The Prophet’s ﷺ invoking curses in qunut for a month recalls which deed for us today?
o: Setting out in anger to take revenge on one’s own
Thinking that making du‘a just once is enough
Being regular and continuous in du‘a against injustice
Only patiently staying silent without making du‘a

porbos.title: The Plot to Drop a Stone • The Order of Expulsion • Departing to Music • The Hypocrites’ Empty Promise • Final Word

blocks.0: The Plot to Drop a Stone
blocks.1: Banu al-Nadir were one of the three main Jewish tribes of Madinah, living in a fortified area on the outskirts of the city. After the Prophet {{1}} came to Madinah a security pact had been made with them, on the condition of not attacking one another.{{2}}
blocks.2: ‘Amr ibn Umayyah (RA) was returning from Bi’r Ma‘unah as a captive. The chief plotter of the treachery at Bi’r Ma‘unah was ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl, a man of the tribe of Banu ‘Amir. On the way, finding two different men of Banu ‘Amir asleep, ‘Amr (RA) killed them, thinking this was revenge for Bi’r Ma‘unah. But these two had no connection with ‘Amir ibn al-Tufayl; the Prophet {{1}} himself had separately given them a pledge of security, which ‘Amr did not know. When he returned to Madinah and told what had happened, the Prophet {{2}} said, I must pay the blood money for these two.{{3}}
blocks.3: Banu al-Nadir had an old alliance pact with Banu ‘Amir; in such pacts there was a custom of helping one another with blood money. On this basis the Prophet {{1}} went to them, to ask for help with the blood money. They said with their mouths, certainly, Abu al-Qasim, we will help as you wish. Then they plotted among themselves. They said, you will never find this man in such a state again. Who will go up on the roof of this house, drop a stone on him, and end the trouble? The Prophet {{2}} was then sitting by the wall of the house of one of them, with him were Abu Bakr (RA), ‘Umar (RA), ‘Ali (RA) and a few Companions. ‘Amr ibn Jihash agreed, climbed up on the roof to drop the stone. News came from heaven to the Prophet {{3}} of what they intended. The plan was to drop the stone on him alone, not on the Companions. He got up and went straight back to Madinah. What he said while getting up is not detailed in the narration; only this much is there, after a while the Companions realized he was not there. The Companions were still sitting by the wall. After a while they realized he was not there. Searching, they met someone on the road to Madinah, who said, I saw him enter Madinah. They went and found him speaking of the Jews’ plot.{{4}}
blocks.4: The very man who had come to them a little while ago to ask for help was the one they were scheming to kill, having made him sit beside their own house’s wall. Treachery is deepest exactly when it comes in the guise of help.
blocks.6: The Prophet {{1}} sent Muhammad ibn Maslamah (RA) to Banu al-Nadir with the order that they leave his protection and the area. The hypocrites then secretly sent word to Banu al-Nadir: stay, take shelter in the fortresses, we will fight with you, if you go out we will go out too. Trusting in that false assurance Banu al-Nadir replied, we will not leave Madinah, do what you will.{{2}}
blocks.7: The Prophet {{1}} surrounded their fortresses with an army. He left Ibn Umm Maktum (RA) in charge of Madinah. The siege went on for some days. Banu al-Nadir shot arrows from inside the fortress. The Muslims began cutting the date palm groves around them, to increase the pressure. Banu al-Nadir shouted, Muhammad, you used to forbid corruption, yet you yourself cut date palms and burn them?
blocks.9: Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by Allah’s command, and so that Allah might disgrace the disobedient.{{1}}
blocks.10: What looks like corruption in the enemy’s eyes may be a just strategy in Allah’s eyes. Who is speaking, their intention and position decides it, not merely the sight of the act.{{1}}
blocks.11: Within a few days of siege Banu al-Nadir’s courage broke. Allah poured fear into their hearts. The hypocrites who had promised help did not move an inch.
blocks.13: He it is who expelled those of the People of the Book who disbelieved from their homes at the first gathering. (O Muslims!) You did not imagine they would go out. They too thought their fortresses would protect them from Allah. Then Allah came upon them from where they had not expected. Allah cast terror into their hearts. So they were demolishing their houses with their own hands and by the hands of the Muslims too. So take a lesson, O people of insight!{{1}}
blocks.14: Banu al-Nadir sent a proposal to the Prophet {{1}}: let us be sent out, saving only our lives; we will take what the camels can carry, without weapons. The Prophet {{2}} accepted.{{3}}
blocks.16: Banu al-Nadir took everything that could be taken. They even took down the doors of their houses and loaded them on camels. Some went to Khaybar, some to Sham. Among those who went to Khaybar were Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Kinanah ibn al-Rabi‘ and Huyayy ibn Akhtab. Reaching Khaybar their influence became such that the people there accepted their leadership. In the procession of departure, the daff and flutes played. Women, dressed up and adorned, walked to the rhythm of that music, as if this were no defeat but a march of victory. No tribe of Arabia had seen anyone set out like this, with such pride.{{1}}
blocks.17: The tribe that was leaving its fortresses that day homeless dressed that journey up as glory with music. How much people do to hide defeat. The land, gardens and houses of Banu al-Nadir remained in the Prophet’s {{1}} hands. Without any war.
blocks.19: The wealth that Allah gave to His Messenger from them as ‘fay’, for it you urged neither horses nor camels. But Allah gives His messengers dominion over whom He wills. Allah has power over all things.{{1}}
blocks.21: The wealth that Allah gave to His Messenger from the people of other towns as ‘fay’ belongs to Allah, His Messenger, (the Messenger’s) relatives, orphans, the needy and travellers, so that this wealth may not circulate only among the wealthy among you.{{1}}
blocks.22: A rule, bound in one sentence. That wealth should not go round in the hands of a few people. Even today this principle is relevant, in the home, in society, in the state. The first Muhajirun who had migrated from Makkah received a share of this wealth; the Ansar of Madinah were not in this distribution, because they already had their own houses. The only exception was two Ansari Companions whose poverty had reached the Prophet’s {{1}} ears: Sahl ibn Hunayf (RA) and Abu Dujanah (RA). He gave them a share too.{{2}}
blocks.23: The rule was bound to the division of Muhajirun and Ansar, yet when news of need came, even that division softened. Following a rule and shutting one’s eyes to need are not the same thing. Two from Banu al-Nadir became Muslim, Yamin ibn ‘Umayr (RA) and Abu Sa‘d ibn Wahb (RA). They stayed with their wealth.{{1}}
blocks.25: After Banu al-Nadir left, the Qur’an brought up those hypocrites who had secretly promised help.
blocks.27: Have you not seen the hypocrites, who say to their disbelieving brothers among the People of the Book, if you are expelled we will go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, and if you are fought, we will help you. Allah bears witness, they are utter liars.{{1}}
blocks.28: Great in word, nothing in reality. When Banu al-Nadir were expelled, not a single hypocrite went out with them. The Qur’an had said beforehand that this would happen.
blocks.30: Indeed if they are expelled they will not go out with them; and if they are fought they will not help them, and if they do come to help they will surely turn their backs and flee. Then they will not be helped.{{1}}
blocks.31: Why does this happen? Allah Himself answered.
blocks.33: In truth fear of you is greater in their hearts than fear of Allah. That is because they are a people who have no understanding.{{1}}
blocks.34: A person who fears people more than Allah, their promise from the mouth is lighter than the wind. If the place of fear is not right, courage also does not stand in the right place. A promise from the mouth is easy. Standing beside someone in a hard time, that is the real test. How often we give such words, and forget them when the time to fulfil them comes. With Allah even that empty promise is held on record.
blocks.36: Some pictures remain from this dars of the fourth year AH. A swarm of bees that guarded the body of a martyr. A razor, and a boy on a prisoner’s lap, with which the prisoner proved there was no flaw in his word. Khubayb’s (RA) two rak‘ahs, which are still the custom for martyrs today. One saying of Zayd (RA), in which even a thorn in the Prophet’s {{1}} foot grew greater than his own life.
blocks.37: The seventy Qurra’, who gathered firewood by day and stood in prayer by night. One saying of Haram (RA), I have won, which drew an enemy to Islam. A month of invoking curses, yet no raising the sword for revenge. Banu al-Nadir’s departure to music, behind whose pride defeat was hidden.
blocks.38: And the biggest picture is of Khubayb’s (RA) last moment. Death standing before him, yet no excuse of busyness, he asks for his two rak‘ahs all the same. So take one task with you from today’s dars.
blocks.40: Even standing face to face with death Khubayb (RA) asked for time for two rak‘ahs of prayer; since then the custom of two rak‘ahs before a martyr. Today I will ask myself one question, the voluntary prayers I leave out on the excuse of busyness, if death were to stand before me, would I not make time for exactly those?
blocks.41: Today, even amid my busyness, I will make time and pray two rak‘ahs of voluntary prayer; this small deed I will not give up from today on.

quiz.q: Whom did ‘Amr ibn Umayyah (RA) kill by mistake?
o: Two Jewish leaders of Banu al-Nadir, with whom there had been a disagreement already
Two men of Banu ‘Amir, with whom the Prophet ﷺ had a security pact
Two people of his own tribe
Two known leaders of the hypocrites

quiz.q: What plot did Banu al-Nadir make against the Prophet ﷺ?
o: A plot to mix poison in food
An attempt to set the tent on fire in the dark of night
An attempt to kill him by dropping a stone from the roof
A plan to attack suddenly at night

quiz.q: What is the thread of events from ‘Amr ibn Umayyah’s (RA) mistaken killing to Banu al-Nadir’s plot?
o: Carrying forward the aftermath of a very old personal enmity
A continuing aftermath of a religious debate between the two sides
Looking for a new chance to kill during the very discussion of blood money
The result of a long-standing border dispute over land

quiz.q: What was the reason Banu al-Nadir’s stone-dropping plot failed?
o: The Prophet ﷺ himself, suspecting beforehand, moved away from there
A Companion present saw the plot with his own eyes
Banu al-Nadir themselves drew back at the last moment
Allah informed him of the plot beforehand through revelation

quiz.q: What caution does ‘Amr ibn Umayyah’s (RA) mistaken killing give us today?
o: It is natural to take revenge at once on realizing a mistake
It is always better to hide any big mistake of one’s own
Taking important decisions alone is always best
To verify well before taking a decision under the sway of anger or haste

quiz.q: What does the failure of Banu al-Nadir’s stone-dropping plot teach us today?
o: Even a secret plot never stands before Allah’s help
It is always safe to regard everyone with suspicion
One should not ask anyone for help in times of danger
Taking security measures is actually an unnecessary matter

quiz.q: What lesson does the caution taken during the talks with Banu al-Nadir give in today’s life?
o: Avoiding all kinds of talks when there is suspicion
Keeping courtesy and caution together even with apprehension
Never giving the opponent any chance in any situation
Taking being cautious to be a sign of rudeness

quiz.q: Who delivered the order to leave Madinah to Banu al-Nadir?
o: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)
‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) himself
Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA)
Muhammad ibn Maslamah (RA)

quiz.q: During the siege, what did the Muslims begin cutting of Banu al-Nadir’s?
o: Date palms
Vineyards
Wheat fields
Walls

quiz.q: Which verse was revealed regarding the cutting of the date palms?
o: Surah al-Hashr 59:7
Surah al-Hashr 59:5
Surah al-Baqarah 2:204
Surah al-Hashr 59:11

quiz.q: Though cutting date palms is generally disliked, what was the reasoning for allowing it in this war?
o: A necessary military tactic to break the enemy’s resistance
Merely the aim of punishing the enemy extra
The aim of greatly increasing the amount of spoils after the war
The aim of making the land permanently their own

quiz.q: What principle of justice does the decision of conditional expulsion given to Banu al-Nadir signify today?
o: Showing even the slightest leniency toward the enemy is a kind of great weakness
Cancelling all conditions altogether is true justice
Keeping the response within reasonable limits even amid enmity
Taking revenge is the only right way here

quiz.q: Which principle does the verse about the permission to cut date palms recall for us today?
o: Every rule always stays completely unchangeable for all time
Any kind of harm is lawful if needed
Destruction is the only possible form of strategy
An exception even to a general rule can be lawful for a specific need

quiz.q: What did Banu al-Nadir play when departing Madinah?
o: Drum and cymbals
Horn blasts
Daff and flute
A stringed harp

quiz.q: How, according to Surah al-Hashr, was Banu al-Nadir’s wealth acquired?
o: At the cost of fierce war and heavy bloodshed
Through a separate peace treaty
By buying it with cash
Neither by urging horses nor camels (without war)

quiz.q: What effect did Banu al-Nadir’s wealth coming into hand without fighting have on the rules of distributing fay’ (wealth apart from war spoils)?
o: The whole wealth was at once deposited fully in the Bayt al-Mal
An instruction came to distribute it by a separate rule, not to ordinary fighters
The soldiers who took part in the war divided all of it among themselves
The wealth was returned to Banu al-Nadir

quiz.q: What principle of wealth distribution in society today does the verse on fay’ distribution state?
o: That wealth should not circulate only among the wealthy
Giving everyone in society wealth in exactly equal shares is obligatory
Establishing the state’s absolute right over all wealth
That there should be no rule at all in wealth distribution

quiz.q: What does the whole sequence of Banu al-Nadir’s expulsion show us today about the consequences of treachery?
o: Treachery is actually never punished
Every breach of a treaty always receives the same punishment
The fruit of breaking a pact, even if late, one day arrives
The punishment for breach of a pact always descends immediately

quiz.q: In verse 11 of Surah al-Hashr, which promise of the hypocrites is mentioned?
o: To go out together if they were expelled
Not to help directly in war
To spy on behalf of the Jews
To secretly betray the Muslims

quiz.q: What did Allah bear witness about the hypocrites’ promise?
o: They are merely hesitant
They are utter liars
They are merely cowardly and weak
They are merely ignorant

quiz.q: Why does the verse hint that the hypocrites in the end stayed absent despite promising help to Banu al-Nadir?
o: They had never found out the right time of the fight
Just at that time they themselves were being attacked elsewhere
Their promise was actually mere hollow lies
The Prophet ﷺ himself had stopped them from going

quiz.q: From the story of the hypocrites’ empty promise, what match between word and deed are we taught to keep today?
o: It is safe not to give any promise to avoid trouble
To fulfil in practice, to the end, the promise given by mouth
Forgetting a promise given at the moment of danger is natural
Keeping spoken word and real action separate is easy
